t: A vibration magnetometer consists of two identical bar magnets placed one over the other such that they are perpendicular and bisect each other. Initially magnetic moment of system M₁=√(M²+M²)=√2M and moment of inertia I₁=I+I=2I
Finally when one of the magnet is removed then M₂=M and I₂=I
So, T=2π√(I/MB_H)
T₁/T₂=√(I₁/I₂×M₂/M₁)=√(2I/I×M/√2M)
⇒T₂=(2^(5/4))/(2^(1/4))=2sec

t: The magnetic field at the point of intersection of diagonals of a square loop of side L carrying a current I is
s:
Refer to Fig. Here r=OE=L/2
[[img:907682238130]]
The magnetic field at the centre O due to the current element AE is given by
B_(AE)=−μ₀I/4πr∫_(90°)^(45°) sinθdθ
=μ₀I/4πr|cosθ|_(90°)^(45°)
=μ₀I/4πr(cos45°−cos90°)
=μ₀I/4πr(cos45°−0)=μ₀I/4√2πr
It is clear that the magnetic field at O due to current element DE is the same as that due to AE. Hence, the magnetic field at O due to one side AD is
B_(AD)=2μ₀I/4√2πr=√2μ₀I/4πr
Since the centre of the square is equidistant from the ends A,B,C and D of each side of the square and each side produces at the centre O the same magnetic field, the field due to the square is 4 times that due to one side. Hence (because r=L/2)
B=4B_(AD)=√2μ₀I/πr=2√2μ₀I/πL
Hence the correct choice is (d).

t: Two identical coils carry equal currents and have a common centre, but their planes are at right angles to each other. What is the magnitude of the resultant magnetic field at the centre if the field due to one coil alone is B ?
s:
The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre due to each coil is B. Since the planes of the coils are at right angles to each other, the directions of the fields will be at right angles to each other. Therefore, the resultant field is
Bᵣ=√(B²+B²)=√2B
Hence the correct choice is (c). .

t: A proton with kinetic energy K describes a circle of radius r in a uniform magnetic field. An α-particle with kinetic energy K moving in the same magnetic field will describe a circle of radius
s:
The radius of the circular orbit is given by
r=√2mK/qB
The charge of an α-particle is twice that of a proton and its mass is four times the mass of a proton. Therefore √m/q is the same for both. Hence r will the same for both particles. Thus the correct choice is (b). !

t: An α-particle moving with a velocity v in a uniform magnetic field is moving in a circular path at frequency v called the cyclotron frequency. The cyclotron frequency of a proton moving with a speed 2v in the same magnetic field will be
s:
The cyclotron frequency is given by
v=qB/2πm
It is independent of the speed of the particle and the radius of its circular path. Now v∝q/m. The charge of a proton is half that of an α-particle and the mass of a proton is one-fourth. Therefore, v will be doubled. Hence the correct choice is (d).

The degree of magnetic saturation achieved is equal to 15%. What is the total dipole moment of the sample for a magnetic field of 0.9 T and a temperature of 3 K ? (in J/T)
s:
Initial total magnetic moment at temperature T= 4 K is
m₁=15% of (2.0×10²⁴×1.5×10⁻²³)=4.5JT⁻¹
Now from Curie’s law, we have χ=C/T or  I/H=C/T
where I is magnetization and H is the magnetizing field. If V is the volume of the sample, then by definition, M=I/V and Eq. (i) becomes

If M₂ is the magnetic moment at temperature T₂= 3 K and field H₂=0.9 T, then from Eq. (ii) M₁ and M₂ are related as

t: The magnetic field due to a current carrying circular loop of radius 3 cm at a point on its axis at a distance of 4 cm from the centre is 54μT. The magnetic field (in μT) at the centre of the loop will be

B=μₒIr²/(2(r²+x²)^(3/2)) (1)
Magnetic field at the centre of the coil is given by
B₀=μₒI/2r (2)
Dividing (1) by (2), we get
B₀/B=r³/((r²+x²)^(3/2))
Substituting the values of r and x, we get
B₀/B=125/27
or  B₀=125/27B=125/27×54μT=250μT
